description: Width tiers for Languages — Background Language Learner F-10 Pathway, Years 7–8 band
subject: Languages — Background Language Learner

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at Y7-8 F-10 level. For communicating descriptors: minimum range of interaction types and contexts. For understanding descriptors: minimum range of language features, text types or cultural phenomena engaged with analytically.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope from ACARA elaborations — what a well-taught Y7-8 background language learner F-10 class would have engaged with.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions adding new task contexts (communicating) or new phenomena (understanding). At Y7-8, real community engagement, interview-based tasks, and cross-cultural analytical work are primary width directions.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations for the Chinese Background Language Learner pathway (Y7-8 F-10 sequence) used as source data.

AC9LCH8C01.minimum_width: Sustain an exchange for at least five turns in a partially or fully unfamiliar context, using at least one maintenance strategy (clarification, paraphrase, or follow-up question); demonstrate at least one real-time language adjustment (rephrasing, register shift, or summarising a peer's view).
AC9LCH8C01.typical_width: Initiate and sustain face-to-face and online exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts; use descriptive language for contrasting perspectives; use persuasive and influencing language; summarise different opinions; request and provide clarification; use digital technology to maintain contact and extend exchanges; contribute to online forums.
wider: Participate in a structured debate or discussion where views must be defended under challenge — demonstrate persuasive language and reasoned position-holding across at least six turns
Reflect on a recorded exchange and identify every moment where language adjustment was or should have been made — discuss what triggered or should have triggered each adjustment
Compare how persuasion and acknowledgement of others' views is managed in target language contexts with Australian conventions
elaborations: initiating and sustaining conversations to share aspects of personal worlds such as recent holidays, future plans or achievements
asking and responding to open-ended questions about learning activities or strategies
sustaining face-to-face and secure online conversations, for example, encouraging responses through questions
using descriptive language to discuss contrasting aspects of personal worlds such as home and school, study and entertainment
using digital technology to maintain contact and exchange thoughts and experiences
requesting repetition or asking for and providing clarification
acknowledging others' ideas and indicating agreement or disagreement in non-judgemental ways
contributing to secure online forums or discussions offering solutions or personal ideas
summarising different opinions in interactions

AC9LCH8C02.minimum_width: Use at least two justification structures during a collaborative planning task; prepare at least five interview questions and conduct an interview with a community member or peer using appropriate target language.
AC9LCH8C02.typical_width: Use justification language in collaborative planning; plan and execute community-facing events and presentations; provide metalanguage-supported peer feedback; conduct community interviews on topics such as migration, life experiences and cultural practices; create resources to help others.
wider: Conduct an interview with a community elder or significant community figure — prepare culturally appropriate questions and present findings for a community audience
Lead the planning of a community-facing event — coordinating all planning, promotion and execution using target language
Prepare and organise a learning activity for peers, encouraging discussion drawn from a range of sources
elaborations: planning and making arrangements for activities such as outings
collaborating to create displays, presentations or performances for family, friends, peers or school community
participating in authentic cultural experiences in the community
collaborating to plan a class activity focused on an environmental or community project
creating posters to promote activities among young people in target language communities
providing feedback using metalanguage to support peers
creating resources to help others, such as helpful hints for new students
conducting interviews with target language community members on topics such as migration and life experiences
preparing and organising a learning activity to engage peers using a range of sources

AC9LCH8C03.minimum_width: Evaluate at least two target language sources using at least two credibility criteria; produce a response to a text that includes both a personal opinion and at least one analytical observation about language, purpose or cultural context.
AC9LCH8C03.typical_width: Access and evaluate credibility of digital and print sources; compare target language and Australian humour; identify register differences across formal and informal texts; respond to narratives with empathy and critical stance; keep a reading journal for imaginative texts; respond to First Nations Australian stories in target language.
wider: Compare target language and English humour in equivalent media formats — identify what is shared and what is culturally specific, and discuss what the comparison reveals about cultural values
Listen to or read a First Nations Australian author's story in English and write a summary or analytical response in the target language, reflecting on cultural perspectives
Conduct a research task using target language search tools — compare the perspectives available in target language versus English language sources on the same topic
elaborations: accessing information from a range of sources and responding with a personal action or opinion
using strategies to understand and respond to texts such as articles, conversations and instructions
accessing a range of print and digital texts to collate and present information
listening to or reading First Nations Australian authors' stories in English and writing a summary or report in Chinese
researching information and considering the credibility of websites
responding to a narrative, writing and performing a simple speech by a main character
identifying differences between language use in formal interviews, speeches and everyday conversations
reading a range of imaginative texts and keeping a reading journal to record understanding and responses
comparing Chinese humour with Australian expressions of humour

AC9LCH8C04.minimum_width: Convert at least one informal expression into formal register; interpret at least one exchange demonstrating at least one clarifying or cultural explanation strategy; compose at least one bilingual public text with accurate meaning transfer.
AC9LCH8C04.typical_width: Convert informal spoken language into formal register; interpret for visitors applying clarification and rephrasing strategies; identify translation challenges involving culturally-specific concepts; develop target language glossaries for English texts; compose bilingual texts for public purposes; amend inaccurate public translations.
wider: Identify and amend an inaccurate or culturally inappropriate public translation — explain the error, why it occurred, and produce a corrected version
Create a bilingual community resource with a real community stakeholder — negotiating content and language choices for a dual-language audience
Reflect on own interpreting experience across formal and informal contexts — compare the strategies used in each and discuss what makes formal interpreting more demanding
elaborations: identifying challenges of translating some concepts, developing strategies and discussing questions raised
understanding how to convert informal spoken language into formal register to suit purposes and audiences
interpreting for visitors as appropriate, applying strategies such as clarifying and rephrasing
comparing choices of language and behaviours when communicating in Chinese and English
developing target language glossaries to accompany English texts
discussing and amending inaccurate translations of public signs or notices
using dictionaries to understand subtle differences in how and when words are used
composing bilingual texts for real audiences
reflecting on which words, expressions or gestures should or should not be used when interacting with target language speakers

AC9LCH8C05.minimum_width: Produce a text demonstrating at least two deliberate language manipulation choices with explanation of intended effect; produce a text through a documented drafting process with at least two deliberate revisions.
AC9LCH8C05.typical_width: Manipulate language for effect — persuasive structures, humour, descriptive and emotive language, jingles, wordplay; develop drafting and editing skills; create multimodal presentations using data and statistics; produce promotional materials; create dramatic or humorous performances; develop written and multimodal narrative accounts.
wider: Create a multimodal text for a real external audience — evaluate its effectiveness with that audience and revise based on feedback
Produce a portfolio of drafts showing the development of a single text from first draft to final version, with annotations explaining each revision decision
Collaboratively prepare and present a short dramatic or humorous performance reflecting situations from own cultural environment
elaborations: producing multimodal presentations using tables, maps, charts or graphs to deliver information
producing a poster or digital brochure using persuasive language to promote aspects of life in a target language region
creating spoken or written texts such as advertisements promoting travel
writing a journal entry or contributing to a school newsletter reflecting on a school excursion
creating captions, commentaries or subtitles for short video clips of intercultural experiences
creating jingles or songs by manipulating language to match tunes
adapting stories or films to new settings and contexts
creating the next scene or a new character for target language imaginative texts
creating written and multimodal narrative accounts of historical figures or literary characters
collaborating to prepare and present short dramatic or humorous performances
developing drafting and editing skills considering stylistic and creative features

AC9LCH8U01.minimum_width: Demonstrate comprehension of spoken target language from at least two unfamiliar voices; identify at least two subtle pronunciation differences between own speech and a model and demonstrate a targeted improvement attempt.
AC9LCH8U01.typical_width: Develop tone discrimination for subtle differences; distinguish regional accent features; identify and practise tone change patterns; compare own speech patterns with standard spoken target language; develop comprehension strategies for diverse speeds and clarity levels.
wider: Conduct a systematic self-comparison of recorded speech with a native speaker model — categorise differences and design a targeted practice plan
Investigate a specific regional accent of the target language — describe the key phonological features and explain the comprehension strategies most useful for that variety
Compare own pronunciation with standard spoken target language using news broadcast recordings — identify systematic differences and discuss their origin
elaborations: listening to short interactions between unfamiliar voices at diverse speeds or levels of clarity
developing tone discrimination and identifying subtle differences in pronunciation including regional accents
differentiating pronunciation changes in tone sandhi patterns
comparing own Chinese speech patterns with target language pronunciation and making adjustments
practising ways in which tone varies according to setting and context
noticing and describing differences in accent when listening to speakers from diverse regions

AC9LCH8U02.minimum_width: Create at least three new compound words using known morphemes verified as accurate; produce a text demonstrating at least three complex grammatical structures (modal, tense-expression, or sentence type) correctly.
AC9LCH8U02.typical_width: Use morphological knowledge to create words and confirm using dictionaries or digital tools; use digital input for the writing system; categorise words by common morpheme; use modal verbs, tense markers and auxiliary verbs; apply advanced punctuation; construct affirmative, negative, interrogative and imperative sentences; understand exclamatory sentences and response conventions.
wider: Analyse how tense and aspect are expressed differently in the target language compared with English verb conjugation — create examples demonstrating each pattern and explain the differences
Investigate advanced punctuation conventions in the target language that have no direct English equivalent — explain the function of each and create examples demonstrating correct use
Analyse own extended writing for grammatical accuracy — identify patterns of error or inconsistency and develop a targeted improvement plan
elaborations: using knowledge of components to select a character when inputting the target language digitally
categorising words containing a common morpheme to understand the relationship between morphemes and specific word meanings
applying knowledge of morphemes to create new words and confirming combinations using dictionaries
applying knowledge of punctuation in writing
understanding elements of grammar such as word order and sentence construction
understanding and using verbs to express modality
comparing how tense is expressed in the target language — completion, experience, intention, negation
recognising the purpose and effect of exclamatory sentences as opposed to statements
constructing a range of sentences in affirmative, negative, interrogative and imperative forms
recognising differences in Chinese and English responses to negative tag questions

AC9LCH8U03.minimum_width: Use at least six metalanguage terms correctly across a text or grammar analysis covering both languages; produce a resource or explanation about at least one key language difference for a peer or younger learner.
AC9LCH8U03.typical_width: Use extended metalanguage for text features — paragraphing, conjunctions, sequencing, point of view; compare how ideas are developed in target language and English texts; apply comparative knowledge to access unfamiliar content; teach younger students about key differences using support resources; explore metaphorical versus literal meaning across languages.
wider: Teach younger students about key differences between the target language and English using support resources such as flash cards, diagrams and charts
Analyse a target language text and annotate every grammatical and textual feature using metalanguage — then compare with an English equivalent and identify all structural differences
Investigate a conceptual metaphor that operates differently in the target language and English — explain how each language encodes the concept and discuss what this reveals
elaborations: extending understanding of metalanguage about a range of textual features in target language and English
identifying and comparing language features in target language and English texts
teaching younger students about some key differences between the target language and English using support resources
applying understanding of key features of familiar text types to understand unfamiliar content
exploring the way content is developed in different types of texts
reading samples of formal texts and identifying how language compares with everyday speech
exploring metaphorical and literal meaning in target language and English texts

AC9LCH8U04.minimum_width: Identify at least two ways attitudes, beliefs or values shape communication in the target language community; reflect on at least one experience of navigating between cultural communities, identifying at least one stereotyping risk and a strategy for avoiding it.
AC9LCH8U04.typical_width: Consider how attitudes, beliefs and values are reflected in language and gesture; reflect on the influence of the target language culture on own communication style; examine cultural practices across regions and diaspora contexts; explore First Nations Australians' language connections to Country; develop awareness of stereotyping in intercultural interactions.
wider: Examine in Chinese or English how First Nations Australians' languages have strong connections to Country/Place and compare these with the ways language connects to cultural identity in the target language community

Analyse a case of cultural misinterpretation — identify the stereotyping or assumption at work, explain the cultural logic of both sides, and discuss how the misunderstanding could have been prevented
Investigate how own family's cultural practices have changed across generations — identify what has been maintained, what has changed, and discuss the factors that drive cultural continuity or change
elaborations: considering how attitudes, beliefs and values can be reflected in language and gesture
reflecting on the influence of target language culture on own communication style
reflecting on participation in cultural events noting similarities and differences across contexts and regions
examining how First Nations Australians' languages have strong connections to Country/Place and comparing with language connections in target language culture
comparing cultural elements reflected in language use and social norms such as body language, volume and silence
recognising that some target language social behaviours may be misinterpreted as lack of courtesy
developing self-awareness of possible stereotyping during interactions
discussing how family origins reflect language use, such as mixing languages while speaking
